items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to directing the New
York state energy research and development authority to study and make
recommendations regarding siting renewable energy resources at decommissioned
or dormant electric generating sites; and directs the New York state energy
research and development authority to issue a request for proposal in support
of a renewable energy project at a dormant electric generating site
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1829

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to directing the
New York state energy research and development authority to study and
make recommendations regarding siting renewable energy resources at
decommissioned or dormant electric generating sites; and directs the New
York state energy research and development authority to issue a request
for proposal in support of a renewable energy project at a dormant elec-
tric generating site

 
PURPOSE:

To encourage the reuse of decommissioned or dormant electric generating
sites for renewable energy purposes; this will help the fight against
climate change and help the economies and tax bases of impacted communi-
ties.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Adds a new section 1884 to the public authorities law that
directs the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority

(NYSERDA) to prepare a report, in consultation with the Public Service
Commission and Empire State Development Corporation, containing recom-
mendations for siting renewable energy resources and energy storage at
decommissioned or dormant electric generating sites. The report must
include a survey of decommissioned or dormant electric generating sites
around the state, an identification of renewable energy development
opportunities at these sites, an assessment of the impact of repowering
dormant electric generating sites with renewable energy on local employ-
ment and local tax bases, and recommendations for further development of
renewable energy resources and energy storage projects at decommissioned
or dormant electric generating sites.

Section 2: NYSERDA is directed to establish the "repowering with renewa-
ble energy" program to develop renewable energy resources and energy
storage at decommissioned and dormant electric generating facilities.
After the completion of the report required in section 1, NYSERDA is
directed to issue a request for proposals through the New York Green
Bank for a repowering with renewable energy project at the Lovett Power
Plant in Rockland County. After the selection of a successful bid for
the repowering with renewable energy project at Lovett, the authority
shall, as appropriate, open solicitations for additional repowering with
renewable energy projects around the state.

Section 3: Effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York is working to become a leader in the fight against climate
change. Around the state, many older fossil fuel power plants have
either been decommissioned or are used only as "peaker" plants, active
for a few days a year. The loss of these power plants has often had
severe impacts on the health of the local economy and strength of the
tax base in impacted communities. However, these sites may provide the
ideal location for development of renewable energy sources as they are
already fully connected into the power distribution network.  This bill
directs NYSERDA to produce a report analyzing the feasibility of siting
renewable energy sources at decommissioned or dormant electric generat-
ing sites and to issue a request for proposals for a pilot project at
the Lovett Power Plant in Rockland County. The repurposing of this site
for renewable energy would bring tremendous benefit to the taxpayers and
economy of northern Rockland, and would provide an example for reusing
other generating sites for renewable energy.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020 - S7952 Referred to Energy and Telecommunications

Assembly

2020 - A10094 Referred to Energy

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to directing the New
York state energy research and development authority to prepare a report
regarding the replacement of decommissioned or dormant electric generating
sites with renewable energy development and energy storage opportunities
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1829B

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to directing the
New York state energy research and development authority to prepare a
report regarding the replacement of decommissioned or dormant electric
generating sites with renewable energy development and energy storage
opportunities

 
PURPOSE:

To encourage the reuse of decommissioned or dormant electric generating
sites for renewable energy purposes; this will help the fight against
climate change and help the economies and tax bases of impacted communi-
ties.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends section 1902 the public authorities law
by as it relates to directing the New York State Energy Research and
Development Authority (NYSERDA) to prepare a report, within 18 months,
surveying decommissioned or dormant electric generating sites, identify-
ing opportunities of development of renewable energy resources and ener-
gy storage on those locations and providing an assessment of the econom-
ic impact of siting renewable energy projects at such locations.

Section two relates to the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCES BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED BILL:

Section of public authorities law being amended has been changed from
section 1884 to section 1902 in order to place the report under the
Build Ready program under NYSERDA.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York is working to become a leader in the fight against climate
change. Around the state, many older fossil fuel power plants have
either been decommissioned or are used only as "peaker" plants, active
for a few days a year. The loss of these power plants has often had
severe impacts on the health of the local economy and strength of the
tax base in impacted communities. However, these sites may provide the
ideal location for development of renewable energy sources as they are
already fully connected into the power distribution network.  This bill
directs NYSERDA to produce a report analyzing the feasibility of siting
renewable energy sources at decommissioned or dormant electric generat-
ing sites.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
